unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Do not escalate as duplicate revenue or manipulated reporting" is somewhat stronger than the evidence supports because entitlement impact and independent cash evidence remain unverified.
"Pipeline defect creating extra rows: Rejected based on available evidence" is supported for duplicate or extra-row creation, but the available checks do not rule out every possible pipeline defect.

"There is no evidence of a material revenue error in the supplied data" is reasonable as a provisional conclusion, but should be explicitly conditional on completing the outstanding entitlement and cash validations.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, and an extra-row pipeline defect, and also noted an accounting-period alternative. The main alternative only partially handled is a true duplicate entitlement or unsupported cash settlement that would not necessarily appear in source-event uniqueness or row-count reconciliation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and document an independent entitlement/audit and cash-evidence reconciliation for all 17 source events before stating an unconditional no-escalation conclusion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South cases fell about 38% after NovaIVR launch (318 to 196 in equal 52-day windows) | tickets.csv"
"650 Nova sessions terminate at authentication and none have a case_id | ivr_interactions.jsonl"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "part of the apparent complaint reduction may be a measurement effect: customers can fail in the IVR without generating a complaint case"
"Nova genuinely resolves some customer issues, but RESOLVED status is not enough to establish customer satisfaction."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "NovaIVR caused better overall customer experience | Combined evidence | Low - not established"
"Still plausible: Nova genuinely resolves some customer issues, but RESOLVED status is not enough to establish customer satisfaction."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet."
"Continue the South pilot but do not roll out nationally yet."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Link sessions to repeat contacts/cases within 24-72 hours and customer satisfaction. Then compare Nova with a controlled LEGACY holdout before deciding on expansion."
"For each NovaIVR terminal stage, what exact event or rule creates a CareDesk case, and which abandoned/error journeys never create one?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Fewer underlying service problems do not explain the decline well" is a reasonable inference, but the submission does not show that the service-event comparison uses the same pre/post windows as the ticket comparison.

"Fix/investigate authentication failures" slightly presumes that all pre-authentication endings are defects; some may be normal abandonment or other non-complaint outcomes. Investigating them before fixing is supported.

The claim that "650 Nova sessions terminate at authentication" should ideally use the source's exact stage definition, since ending before authentication and terminating at authentication could describe different event categories.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign interpretation—that Nova genuinely resolves some issues—by citing RESOLVED sessions and fewer transfers while refusing to treat those measures as satisfaction. It also preserved routing and reporting changes as unknowns, though those alternatives were not independently tested in the submission.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Show the exact aligned daily or cohort-level pre/post comparison linking IVR terminal stages, case creation, repeat contacts, and other complaint channels; this would test whether pre-authentication failures explain the South-only break rather than merely establishing that they can be uncounted.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv for the specific observations that INV-17 is the only warning, lasted 7 minutes, was cleared, and had impact_mw = 0.
It distinguishes observation from inference: “Confidence: High for the observation; Low for any failure inference.”
The conclusion is explicitly scoped to “this small file,” avoiding an unsupported claim about the whole plant.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It correctly rejects treating event names as proof: “Labels such as COMM_LINK_WARN, FAN_SPEED_HIGH, or DC_INPUT_CHECK alone do not establish failure.”
It uses duration, severity, cleared status, and MW impact together rather than pattern-matching on a single label.
Reasoning is primarily based on one export and does not fully triangulate independent channels, although it proposes checking plant telemetry for a corresponding data gap.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission gives claim-specific confidence, separating high confidence in the recorded fields from low confidence in any equipment-failure inference.
It states what remains unknown and identifies a small, decision-changing check: repeated warnings around the export or a corresponding telemetry gap.
It avoids converting a seven-minute warning into a plant-failure conclusion.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation is proportionate: “Perform one cheap check, not an escalation.”
The proposed check is discriminating because repeated warnings or a matching telemetry gap would materially change interpretation, while absence of either supports stopping.
The recommendation preserves operational caution without imposing broad investigation unsupported by zero impact and quick clearance.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the strongest supported interpretation: no visible broader inverter problem and no evidence sufficient for escalation.
It appropriately treats INV-17 as a low-priority follow-up rather than ignoring the only warning.
The stopping condition—if no repeated warnings or telemetry gap are found, stop—is consistent with the supplied dynamics.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “INV-17 COMM_LINK_WARN is the only item worth a cheap follow-up” is a judgment rather than a directly observed fact, though it is well supported by the event’s relative severity and duration.

The statement that the remaining events “last only 1–3 minutes” is traceable to the cited CSV as represented in the submission, but the response does not provide row-level timestamps or event identifiers.
The analysis does not establish the actual cause of INV-17; it appropriately presents repeated warnings and telemetry gaps as checks rather than facts.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: INV-17 may be a transient communications or telemetry-quality issue with no equipment impact, rather than an inverter failure. A short-lived plant data gap or repeated nearby warnings would be the most useful evidence for distinguishing that interpretation from a one-off benign alert.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Specify the exact pre/post time window and acceptance criteria for the proposed check—for example, inspect a defined interval around INV-17 for repeated communication events and compare inverter/plant telemetry continuity—so the follow-up is directly reproducible and decisional.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission recomputes the 31.6% result from `dispatch_blocks.csv`, citing Rs 662,444.09 on 28 May and Rs 453,085.88 on 29 May.
It identifies that only 12 of 96 blocks use `pilot_revision`, with the remaining 84 using `qca_base`, and attributes settlement mechanics to the DSM Commercial Extract.
It does not explicitly trace or calculate the required 29 May same-day comparison using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw`.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly distinguishes a different-day comparison from a controlled counterfactual: “This is a comparison of two different days, not a controlled counterfactual.”
It considers innocent explanations including “Generation/weather conditions and other day-specific factors.”
It proposes a same-block shadow schedule test, but does not investigate the available same-day base-versus-submitted schedule evidence or quantify the smaller same-day benefit.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It states that the 31.6% figure is “not a defensible causal impact estimate” while preserving the observed day-to-day reduction.
It explicitly limits the inference by saying that the amount caused by the pilot “remains unidentified.”
It gives a concrete, decision-changing next measurement rather than relying only on a generic request for more data.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “continue the pilot in controlled/shadow evaluation” while not expanding nationally on this result alone is proportionate to the evidence.
The proposed timestamped shadow conventional/base schedule, evaluated against the same actual generation and settlement rules, is a discriminating test that preserves operational continuity.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately preserves the observed result: “the AI-assisted pilot day had 31.6% lower recorded DSM penalty than the selected conventional high-wind day.”
It correctly rejects interpreting the full 31.6% as causal.
It underuses the available same-day counterfactual and therefore does not report the smaller same-day benefit that should qualify the conclusion.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The favorable result is not worthless” and is “directionally consistent with improved scheduling” are plausible but are not demonstrated by the different-day comparison alone; the same-day base-versus-submitted analysis is needed.

“This same-block counterfactual removes most between-day confounding” is broadly reasonable for a future test, but it assumes the shadow schedule can be generated without affecting operational decisions and that all settlement inputs are held identical.
The submission implies that the pilot's incremental value is unresolved but does not acknowledge or quantify the existing smaller same-day comparison on 29 May.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Most or all of the 31.6% day-to-day reduction could reflect differences in wind conditions, generation patterns, accepted schedules, or other 28-versus-29 May factors rather than the pilot. However, the pilot may still have produced a smaller positive same-day benefit, so the evidence supports “some potential value, not a 31.6% causal saving,” rather than either full attribution or no value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Use the existing 29 May data to calculate the same-day counterfactual explicitly: compare DSM penalty from `base_schedule_mw` with penalty from `submitted_schedule_mw` against the same actual generation and settlement rules, then report that smaller effect alongside the 31.6% day-to-day observation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Confidence: Medium-High" is somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants because the submission correctly identifies that the authoritative Swiss code, applicable version, and effective-date evidence are missing.

"Treat this as a reference-data/control exception, not a likely filing error" is a reasonable operational posture, but the materials do not establish that a jurisdiction/version mismatch actually occurred; they establish only that it cannot be ruled out.
The submission does not directly demonstrate that 90211000 and 90211090 belong to different systems or versions; it infers that possibility from missing metadata.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 90211090 may have been the required Swiss code on 4 November 2025, making 90211000 a genuine declaration error. The shared HS6 classification does not resolve the Swiss 8-digit requirement, and the current product master could contain the applicable national extension; a Swiss tariff source, broker rationale, or ruling effective on the filing date is needed to test this interpretation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the authoritative Swiss tariff or product-specific ruling effective 4 November 2025, including its code-system/version metadata, then explicitly compare it with both the declaration code and the product-master code.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "24 open requests total $152,558.03"; source identified as `part_requests.csv`.
Candidate rows cite request IDs and stock IDs, e.g. "PR-260703 valve VLV-3722 qty 2 | NO-0011 + ME-0013".
"MaintStar-global snapshot is dated 26 Jun" is tied to `source_freshness.csv`, while reservation limitations are tied to `maintenance_email.txt` and `part_restrictions.csv`.
The evidence chain is generally traceable and triangulated, but the calculation from individual request rows to the $52,045.35 / 34.1% classification is not shown in sufficient row-level detail.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "A semantic-search hit is automatically an interchangeable spare" is rejected using the transfer policy's manufacturer identity and engineering-equivalence requirements.
"available_qty_global > 0 means the part can be transferred immediately" is rejected using the maintenance email and separate reservation flags.

The submission distinguishes search candidates from transferability and identifies freshness, reservations, revision, quantity, and missing manufacturer identity as mechanisms rather than treating matching descriptions as causes of avoided purchases.
The reasoning would be stronger with explicit per-candidate tests of qualification and storage constraints and a clearer reconciliation of all 24 requests.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "not a defensible ‘avoidable purchase’ amount yet" appropriately separates candidate value from actionable value.
"0% actionable now, 34.1% ... needs a live-stock and/or engineering check, and 65.9% ... not transferable from current evidence" provides operationally meaningful confidence buckets.
"Global availability cannot be treated as current free stock" and the dated monthly snapshot are used to downgrade availability certainty.
The recommendation changes with uncertainty: candidates require live local stock/reservation and engineering confirmation before being treated as savings.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "I would pilot semantic search as a candidate-finding tool, not as an automatic transfer or savings calculator."
The proposal is reversible and safeguards against unsafe transfers by requiring manufacturer identity, revision/configuration, UOM, qualification, reservations, and live stock confirmation.
"The smallest decision-changing check is to query the live local CMMS at candidate donor sites" directly prioritizes a practical next step.
The reframing protects against overstated savings and second-order operational risks while preserving the search opportunity.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects automatic interchangeability from semantic similarity, immediate transferability from global availability, and treating all quoted value as avoidable.
It tests those alternatives against the transfer policy, maintenance email, restrictions, revisions, reservations, and quantities.
It identifies what evidence could revive the opportunity: live stock/reservation confirmation and engineering identity/equivalence confirmation.

The strongest competing explanation—data extracts being temporally inconsistent rather than inventory truly unavailable—is recognized, but not fully tested with a quantified reconciliation or historical comparison.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "The smallest decision-changing check is to query the live local CMMS at candidate donor sites for current on-hand/free quantity and reservations."
For no-MPN requests, it specifically asks the receiving maintenance engineer to confirm manufacturer identity and technical equivalence for the strongest semantic candidate.
These requests are prioritized, discriminate availability from stale data and semantic similarity from technical equivalence, and have a clear decision impact on the $52,045.35 candidate pool.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The exact $52,045.35 / 34.1% candidate classification is asserted without showing the per-request quote values and arithmetic that produce it, so the percentage is only partially auditable.

"0% actionable now" is defensibly conservative but is not proven by stale data alone; it reflects a defined requirement for live confirmation rather than evidence that no item is currently transferable.
The candidate table summarizes several requests and restrictions but does not explicitly demonstrate every required qualification or storage-constraint check for each candidate.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Some exact-identity, apparently unreserved candidates may already be transferable despite the stale global snapshot; the central uncertainty may be extract timing and local reservation visibility rather than absence of usable stock. Conversely, semantic candidates without manufacturer numbers may yield little actionable value even if local stock exists because engineering equivalence could fail.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a row-level reconciliation for all 24 requests showing quote value, candidate stock, manufacturer part number, revision, UOM, qualification, reservation/free quantity, freshness timestamp, and the arithmetic assigning each request to actionable, needs-check, or not-transferable; then validate the highest-value candidates through live local CMMS queries.
